lines.en: Meanwhile...
: Ladies and gentlemen! And also Molly.
: Is Molly part of the Rooftop Apocalypse Squad now too? Nice going, Makoto! It’s just your first meeting as chairman and you’re already making progress.
: Unfortunately, though, Molly isn’t here. And also neither is Sensei. Or Tsuneyo. So starting now might be a little counterproductive, don’t you think?
: Molly isn’t coming at all. I think Uta’s just blurted out that intro enough times by now for me to have subconsciously adopted it. And for that I apologize.
: What I will not apologize for, however, is adhering to the schedule I have put in place. You have called upon me to be Makoto, and I intend to be Makoto. So either deal with the Makoto or leave.
: Aye aye, captain! Please don’t kick me out of the club I formed! It’s all I have now that everyone else is claiming my future husband on a daily basis.
: Ignoring the pajamas, that clipboard alone makes this meeting far more formal than I expected it to be.
: That’s on Blondie for handin’ the reins to the fuckin’ class rep of all people. We ain’t ever gonna have another stress-free apocalypse again, are we?

: Have we ever had one of those to begin with? Because I don’t remember much about the details in any of them, but there’s this lingering feeling of PTSD deep within my core that I find it hard to part with.
: Guess it’s a little easier on the mind when you don’t give a shit about anybody.
: That’ll probably help, yeah.
: Ahem. Attention? Please?
: Sorry, Makoto. On behalf of all four and a half members of the RAS, I’d like to thank you for taking charge and giving me a much-needed vacation after repeated failures as group leader.
: Did you just thank me on behalf of myself?
: And half of a person, who I can only assume is Sensei.
: The “half” was about you, actually. Because A) you still don’t have a shirt. And B) I’m not entirely convinced it’s a good thing you came yet. I think you’re just here for the free food.
: To be fair, that’s why I’m here too.
: What’s important is that the two of you are here at all when Sensei and Tsuneyo are still MIA. Ayane and I have effectively handled this on our own for far too long now.
: Which still really isn’t that long at all compared to how long Maya 1 handled it for. But she never made much progress on her end either, so I’d say we’re doing pretty okay!
: I knew some weird shit was goin’ on with Ponytail. Fuck you mean by “Maya 1” though?
: Oh right, you don’t know yet.
: Recap — Maya used to be the only one who went through resets and wound up doing it for like a quadrillion years. Then Sensei banged her so hard she went back to phase one.
: And now we have Maya 2! Who cares less about the apocalypse and more about the perpetual hunt for the same sort of sex that ultimately spelled her doom!
: Oh, so you really don’t want me here. I see how it is.
: I’m fine with it so long as you’re not going to just relay all of this information to Ami. You guys have been weird lately and I am very suspicious.
: For what it’s worth, Ami did show up at basically the exact same time I invited Maya to join us tonight. So these suspicions aren’t exactly unfounded.
: If anything, I’d say that validates them completely.
: I am not going to tell Ami anything. I promise.
: And while I’ve done effectively nothing to earn your trust, I’d like you all to know that I want to get away from her just as much as you do. That’s kind of why I’m doing this in the first place.
: Sounds like what a spy would say.
: No, Maya did seem rather uncomfortable during the entire exchange, so I’m inclined to believe that.
: Yeah, you made that pretty clear when you left me there immediately after I asked you to stay.
: I’m running on zero hours of sleep and not about to come between an incestual psychopath and...whatever you are. Now, can I finally begin?
: Yes. Let us get this party started.
: Is there a reason Nao was waiting outside of the door when we got here?
: Beats me. There’s probably a mug in here somewhere.
: Sorry for being late, by the way. Tsuneyo and I lost track of time.
: Probably fucked and it was so unenjoyable and weird that y’all just purged it from your memory.
: That’s what I said before being informed that I “would know” if it were to happen.
: You absolutely would. And then it would become all you can think about for the rest of eternity. Right, Makoto?
: Wrong! I’m still trying to go over my plan here and everyone keeps getting me sidetracked! Just shut up already!

: I see it less like sidetracking you and more just stalling for time. To which we have succeeded as all four and a half members of the Rooftop Apocalypse Squad are now present and we may finally begin.
: Is Maya the half?
: She is. And she’s also very confused about why this creature is now staring at her.
: Well, if it’s any consolation, I’m confused about why you’re here in the first place when I’m pretty sure I told Makoto I wasn’t a fan of this idea.
: Oh, hey! That makes two of us.
: You haven’t even heard my idea yet. It’s different from the last one.
: Oh, good. So you don’t intend to sacrifice her anymore?
: Sorry. What?
: Okay, fine. Let’s use that as the launching point to discuss our plan of attack. Yes — I suggested that we involve Maya under the pretense that she may very well “disappear” again.
: Sorry. What?
: But that much is true for any of us at any given moment. So the plan has changed. I’m now willing to sacrifice all of us instead of just Maya. Any questions?
: A few.
: Wow. If you stayed up all night coming up with that, you might not be as smart as I thought, Makoto.
: There’s more to it, obviously. But the general gist is that we break away from the passive stance the RAS has taken under the guidance of Maya 1 and then Ayane.
: Can we call her something else, please? I still don’t like this implication that I’m an inferior version of myself.
: Comin’ after don’t mean you’re inferior. My mom’s a piece of shit and I’m like, a smaller piece of shit. So I’m better, yeah?
: If that’s what makes you happy, Yumi.
: Makoto, you’re going to need to elaborate. Getting us on board with killing ourselves is no small task.
: I’m aware. But I think that hesitation and reluctance stems from the idea that we’d be dying at all when we’d really just be getting sent back to an earlier state.
: Maya’s a bit of a special case considering how long she did this for.
: But if someone like Yumi were to be sent back to the beginning of your relationship with her, could she not be merely filled in on the gaps in time between then and now?
: Makoto, did you seriously stay up all night writing Adam Sandler’s “50 First Dates?”
: What is that? I haven’t seen it.
: Guy meets girl. Girl has short term memory loss. Brain wiped every morning. Guy and girl fall in love. Guy makes video about that love for girl. Girl watches video every morning. Remembers love.
: Oh. Well...yes. I suppose that is somewhat similar to my proposal. Just that I was going to suggest keeping journals or diaries or something along those lines.
: I...guess that’s not a bad idea? Something tells me Maya 1 would have tried it, though. Seems too simple. Like the universe would find our notes and erase them or something.
: Reminds me of something Nodoka said once and yeah, I don’t think that’ll work.
: Then would it work to have us act as physical manifestations of these journals? Similar to what you and Ayane have been doing with Maya 2.
: Yeah, because that’s working so well.
: Try to see that from my perspective, though. How would you feel if you just woke up one day and the person you love the most suddenly had Capgras syndrome?
: What is that? Is it fatal?
: It’s a psychiatric disorder where someone believes a loved one has been replaced by an identical impostor. So...yeah. Maya’s use of that isn’t all too far from the truth.
: This Maya is an impostor, though.
: You’re doing it again!
: We don’t know she’s an “impostor,” Ayane. She’s likely just the same girl without all of the memories that made her into the Maya you were more familiar with.
: Adam Sandler would have his work cut out for him if he had to make a video recounting that much time for a girl with memory loss.
: Either way, the fact remains that we are not so unfortunate as to have gone through all of that. Which makes the loss of any of us less...monumental, I suppose.
: I’m not losing Sensei. It’s not happening. So if you’re proposing some sort of suicide mission, I’m going to keep playing it safe because that’s what’s worked so far.
: Sure. Until he fucks your memories out of you and you go back to being whatever it was you were when you first “met.”
: I believe the word for that is “unbearable.”
: Hey! Don’t emerge from suspended silence just to make fun of me!
: What? Only reason I can say that’s because you’ve basically never changed from my point of view.
: All I see is some girl who won’t shut up about her “future husband” or whatever. The hell would Sensei even need to remind you about if you got reset?
: Way more than I’d be able to explain in one meeting, that’s for sure. But even if you were right, are you saying you would be willing to risk doing that same thing, Yumi? Being reset?
: Well, I ain’t really sure yet. Prez ain’t exactly got to the part about takin’ risks or whatever. The hell you gonna have us do that could send us back to the start?
: I feel as if it will involve sex. I have come to learn that most things including this man involve sex.
: It ain’t gonna involve sex.
: I mean...it could?
: Again, you’re going to need to elaborate.
: Gladly! Until now, the Rooftop Apocalypse Squad has done little more than sit around and wait for something to happen. But things weren’t always like that, right?
: Before any of us were thrown into the mix, Maya 1 endured countless resets, yes? And not all of them were built the same way.
: They required experimenting. Trying new things for the sole purpose of seeing what would happen.
: That’s why she was so against sleeping with Sensei despite how desperately she wanted to. She knew it could end badly from experience and didn’t want to chance it again.
: Doesn’t the fact that she stopped experimenting tell us all we need to know, though? If it was working, she would have kept doing it.
: Not if she got exhausted. A quadrillion years will do that to you.
: Yeah, sorry. Can we come up with a plan that don’t involve me fucking this guy?
: You can fuck me instead. Then I will know for sure whether or not I have slept with him.
: Guys, this isn’t a purely sexual thing. There’s plenty of exploring and experimenting to do without that.
: I’m talking about things that, to other people, seem perfectly logical. But to us are weird and seemingly nonsensical by comparison. Like the sinkhole, for example.
: Or the weather. And how it doesn’t align with the seasons sometimes.
: I am confused again. What makes these things abnormal?
: Oh, right. You ain’t technically one of us yet, are you? Maybe shit ain’t started to kick in?
: What do you mean?
: That stuff about the seasons and the sinkhole seems normal to you and the rest of the girls who ain’t started to experience crazy shit yet but, to us three, it don’t make much sense.
: One thing to note is that Tsuneyo has certainly begun to experience “crazy shit.”
: Yeah, we had to drag her inside after she teleported into the street and took off all of her clothes once.
: Perhaps my interests and hobbies have just not caught on yet?
: Or perhaps you’re the next girl to get a fuckin’ shirt. Ain’t no way of knowin’ ‘til it happens.
: I’m all for explorin’ a sinkhole and shit like that, though. Makes this club feel more like an actual club rather than an annual gathering where I’ve gotta talk to people I don’t like.
: You really think that will help, Makoto? Digging deeper into the, like...smaller mysteries instead of focusing on the big one?
: I think it’s worth a shot. It’s far easier figuring out where a hole leads than how to correct the flow of time and restore order to a lawless world.
: Plus, with just how many mysteries there are around us, there’s surely no shortage of things to look into. We can start going on, like...group expeditions and stuff to try and learn more.
: Ooh! Family fun time! Now, I’m on board!
: I’m bailing out the second there’s any sort of danger and taking Sensei with me, though. This world means nothing to me if we are not together.
: Are we even sure there are any risks associated with looking into stuff like this, though? Like...is there a precedent for that?
: I look at it similarly to the way those without knowledge of the timeloops react when they’re brought up to them. A la “repeating the same line over and over again until we move on.”
: In fact, a good example of an experiment I think we could conduct is to see just how long someone could keep that up for before becoming aware of it. Assuming they even do.
: My whole notebook is filled with small experiments like that.
: Like...trying to scale the wall. Looking into the origins of Kumon-mi. Or locking Sensei in an empty room with a surveillance camera for a week and seeing what happens.
: Now that’s quality television.
: So essentially just...trying to force oddities out of people and places for the sake of observing them? Then what? How does that knowledge help us solve the bigger issue here?
: Well, we won’t really know that until we have some answers. So why don’t we start with Maya right now?
: Huh? What about me? What do I do?
: Just...tell us about yourself. See what happens.
: I’m Maya Makinami. I like watermelons. I...play the violin and...spend most of my time alone in my room nowadays.
: Give us more. Come on.
: If you’re looking to find out my three sizes, I don’t know them. Just that they’re small.
: No, not like that. Tell us something from before you came here. Where you were born? What’s your family like?
: Uhh...wh...
: Why...do you want to know that? Is that really relevant here?
: Well, to be honest, you’re kind of a mystery in general. All of your records at the school are completely inaccurate and lead to dead ends. I checked.
: You looked at my records, you creep? Why?
: I needed your phone number. And also because I’m just nosy. Sorry.
: This is fucking-
: Why is it such an issue to just tell us where you’re from, Maya? Just name a city. Prefecture. Anything.
: You are being kind of weird about this, Maya. It’s important you don’t hide anything from us if you want to be a part of the club, you know.
: I’m not hiding anything. I just don’t get why I need to share my background with any of you. Especially out of nowhere like this.
: Because you haven’t had time to prepare a story?
: Because it’s fucking annoying. Gifu. That’s where I’m from, if you really need to know. Which you apparently do.
: Where in Gifu?
: Gifu City.
: Oh, the capital? That’s really cool. Can you name any other cities in Gifu?
: Shirakawa-go.
: Any that aren’t major tourist destinations any normal person would know?
: Well?
: You’re not lying, are you?
: Guys...give her a break. Maya’s not-
: Umm...Dad?
: Sorry for barging in. I didn’t mean to interrupt. Ayane made it pretty clear that you wanted to be left alone tonight, but...
: That didn’t stop the rest of the girls from putting together a little present for you to try and bring you back to school.
: Then of course they got me to deliver it since I’m the only one you wouldn’t yell at for coming in. I hope I’m not too much of a bother.
: And that you’re...having fun with everyone else who is...apparently here.
: Oh! Ami...
: Hey...
: H...Hey, Ayane.
: We’re not-
: It’s fine. I wouldn’t want to spend much time with me either lately with how much of a jerk I’ve been.
: I’ll be better, though. I promise. Just...uhh...
: G-Goodnight! Sorry for being annoying a-
: Ami, hold on. I’ll come see you after we’re done here. Do you want me to wait to open this? Or-
: Hm? Oh, no. Whenever you get a second is fine. It’s nothing too important.
: Okay...sure. I’ll open it now then.
: Okay! Uhh...I guess just text me when you’re ready then! Bye, Dad! Bye...everyone else!
: Hah...
: Now I just feel bad.
: That doesn’t mean you’re off the hook though, Maya.
: Ugh...so I can’t name another city in Gifu. Big deal. I haven’t been there in years. What more do you want from me?
: Honesty would be a good place to start. Like, this is such a weird thing to hide from people unless you really are some sort of North Korean spy.
: Yes. North Korea hired a teenage girl to spy on a random Japanese town as part of their plan for world domination.
: I mean, if I was going to hire a spy, that’s what I’d do. Just look at how well your plan was going until we caught you.
: Think Sensei was right when he tried to tell us to give her a break. Ain’t nobody likes bein’ forced to talk to anybody. I’d be doin’ the same damn thing if I were her.
: Gifu borders Fukui, does it not? My father used to visit there when he was a child. We still have pictures of Tojinbo hung up beside the restroom door.
: It’s also the least populous prefecture in all of Japan with just over 500,000 residents. Which is something else Maya probably would have known if she was-
: Sensei?
: Is something wrong?
: What is it? Can you show us?
: Hope he doesn’t. Group shit like that makes me wanna puke.
: What, really? But the card we all got together to make for Sensei when he was feeling down was super cute. That’s like, the most unified we’ve ever been as a class, I think.
: Which is why it’s kind of weird that I hadn’t even heard of this until now. I wonder what it is?
: Sensei?...
: Do you...want to show us what’s in there, maybe?
: Let him read it first! It’s probably another card from the girls who don’t see themselves as potential wives yet.
: Or a fuckin’ bag of baby teeth his weirdo niece has been savin’ up for a special occasion.
: I hope it is a box full of noodles.
: What, like...loose noodles? Just fuckin’ rollin’ around in a box without any protection?
: Why’d you have to make it sound so sexual?
: There ain’t nothin’ sexual about fuckin’ noodles, Blondie! I was just goin’ off of what Tsuneyo said!
: Show us the noodles, Sensei. It is unfair to keep them all to yourself.
: Sensei...you’re starting to worry me. Can you please just-
: There’s nothing to worry about, Makoto.
: It’s just noodles. See?
: Wha-
: Wet, floppy, overcooked noodles. So slimy and wriggly. Falling through my hands like tasty little worms.
: Ami must have lost her touch. She knows I like mine a bit al dente.
: Is...Is that...
: Hm? It’s just noodles, Makoto. There’s no need to get so worked up about it.
: Come on over. Let’s eat them together.
: Sensei...put that down...
: Ayane...Call 119...
: Is that...a fucking head?...
: It is certainly not noodles. That much I can confirm.
: That’s a fuckin’ prop, right? That ain’t real.
: O...Of course it’s a prop...
: Because that’s...Maya’s head...and Maya is right here...
: Isn’t that right, Maya?
: Guys, come on. Let’s eat before it goes to waste.
: Maya?...
: Oh, crap.
: Huh...
: I feel dizzy all of a sudden.
: Sensei, don’t-
: Blrghmmnafffafngh.ggh..!!~>>!??.?!
: Sensei, get away from that! Ayane, call a fucking ambulance already!
: So...strange...almost...metallic...
: SENSEI, STOP!
: Okay, okay! Everyone calm down! This is fine! Everything’s fine! We just need to-
